label: NestJS Framework
description: A progressive Node.js framework for building efficient, reliable, and scalable server-side applications using modern JavaScript and TypeScript.

children.label: First Steps
children.description: Core fundamentals, prerequisites, and setup instructions for starting a new NestJS project using the Nest CLI.

children.label: Controllers
children.description: Components responsible for handling incoming HTTP requests and returning responses to the client.

children.label: Providers
children.description: Core building blocks in NestJS, such as services, repositories, and factories, designed to be injected as dependencies.

children.label: Modules
children.description: Classes annotated with @Module() used to organize and manage the application structure and dependency graph.

children.label: Middleware
children.description: Functions called before the route handler that have access to request and response objects to execute code or modify payloads.

children.label: Exception Filters
children.description: An exceptions layer responsible for processing all unhandled exceptions and sending user-friendly responses.

children.label: Pipes
children.description: Injectable classes used for data transformation and validation before route handlers are executed.

children.label: Guards
children.description: Injectable classes that implement authorization and determine whether a request can proceed to the route handler.

children.label: Interceptors
children.description: Classes inspired by Aspect-Oriented Programming that bind extra logic before or after method execution and transform results.

children.label: Custom Decorators
children.description: Custom-defined decorators to simplify parameter extraction, improve code readability, and compose multiple decorators.

children.label: Deployment
children.description: Best practices and steps for compiling TypeScript and deploying NestJS applications to production environments.

children.label: Standalone Applications
children.description: A way to bootstrap NestJS without network listeners, wrapping the IoC container for CRON jobs or CLI tools.

children.label: Nest CLI
children.description: The command-line interface tool used to initialize, develop, and maintain NestJS applications.

children.label: CLI Overview & Installation
children.description: Covers the installation of the Nest CLI globally or via npx, and the basic workflow for creating and running projects.

children.label: Workspaces & Modes
children.description: NestJS supports two modes of code organization: standard mode for single projects, and monorepo mode for multi-project workspaces.

children.label: Standard Mode
children.description: The default mode for individual project-focused applications with their own dependencies and settings.

children.label: Monorepo Mode
children.description: A lightweight monorepo structure that coordinates multiple applications and libraries within a single workspace.

children.label: Nest Libraries
children.description: Lightweight, reusable packages within a monorepo workspace that must be imported into an application to execute.

children.label: CLI & Scripts
children.description: Explains how the Nest CLI interacts with compilers (tsc, swc) and package.json scripts to manage the build and execution pipeline.

children.label: Build Process
children.description: The build process wraps tsc, swc, or webpack to compile TypeScript to JavaScript while handling tsconfig-paths.

children.label: Execution Process
children.description: The execution process ensures the project is built and then invokes the node command, supporting watch mode for development.

children.label: CLI Command Reference
children.description: Detailed reference of commands available in the Nest CLI for project creation, generation, and management.

children.label: nest new
children.description: Creates and initializes a new standard mode NestJS project with default configurations and folders.

children.label: nest generate
children.description: Generates and/or modifies files based on a schematic, such as controllers, services, modules, or libraries.

children.label: nest build
children.description: Compiles a NestJS application into a production-ready bundle using the configured compiler.

children.label: nest start
children.description: Compiles and runs a NestJS application, with options for watch mode and debugging.

children.label: nest add
children.description: Imports a library that has been packaged as a Nest library, running its installation schematic.

children.label: nest info
children.description: Displays information about installed Nest framework packages, CLI version, and system environment.

children.label: Fundamentals
children.description: Core fundamental concepts of NestJS, including advanced dependency injection, lifecycle events, testing, and execution contexts.

children.label: Custom Providers
children.description: Advanced dependency injection techniques in NestJS using custom tokens, values, classes, and factories.

children.label: Dependency Injection Fundamentals
children.description: The Inversion of Control (IoC) technique used by NestJS to delegate instantiation of dependencies to the runtime container.

children.label: Asynchronous Providers
children.description: Providers that delay application startup until asynchronous tasks, such as database connections, are completed.

children.label: Circular Dependency
children.description: A situation where two classes depend on each other, requiring special resolution techniques in NestJS.

children.label: Forward Reference
children.description: A utility function forwardRef() that allows NestJS to reference classes which are not yet defined.

children.label: Dynamic Modules
children.description: Modules that can be configured dynamically at runtime, enabling customizable provider registration.

children.label: Injection Scopes
children.description: Mechanisms to control the lifetime and sharing behavior of providers across requests and consumers.

children.label: Default Scope (Singleton)
children.description: The default scope where a single instance of a provider is shared across the entire application lifecycle.

children.label: Request Scope
children.description: A scope where a new instance of the provider is created exclusively for each incoming request and garbage-collected afterward.

children.label: Transient Scope
children.description: A scope where each consumer injecting the provider receives a new, dedicated instance.

children.label: Lazy Loading Modules
children.description: A technique to load modules on-demand to decrease bootstrap time, especially useful in serverless environments.

children.label: Execution Context
children.description: Utility classes providing information about the current execution context across HTTP, RPC, and WebSockets.

children.label: Arguments Host
children.description: An abstraction over a handler's arguments used to retrieve arguments based on the active application context.

children.label: Lifecycle Events
children.description: Hooks provided by NestJS to run code during key application phases: initializing, running, and terminating.

children.label: Module Reference
children.description: The ModuleRef class used to navigate internal providers and dynamically instantiate static or scoped providers.

children.label: Discovery Service
children.description: A utility from @nestjs/core to dynamically inspect and retrieve registered providers and controllers at runtime.

children.label: Platform Agnosticism
children.description: NestJS's design philosophy allowing logical parts to be reused across HTTP, Microservices, WebSockets, and GraphQL.

children.label: Testing
children.description: Built-in testing utilities and integration with Jest and Supertest for unit and end-to-end testing.

children.label: Unit Testing
children.description: Testing individual components in isolation by mocking dependencies using NestJS's testing module.

children.label: GraphQL
children.description: Module cung cấp khả năng tích hợp GraphQL mạnh mẽ vào NestJS, hỗ trợ cả hai phương pháp Code First và Schema First sử dụng Apollo hoặc Mercurius.

children.label: GraphQL Quick Start
children.description: Hướng dẫn cài đặt và cấu hình ban đầu cho GraphQL Module với các driver Apollo hoặc Mercurius.

children.label: Code First Approach
children.description: Phương pháp sử dụng TypeScript decorators và classes để tự động sinh ra GraphQL SDL schema.

children.label: Schema First Approach
children.description: Phương pháp sử dụng GraphQL SDL (Schema Definition Language) làm nguồn chân lý (source of truth) để định nghĩa schema.

children.label: Resolvers
children.description: Các thành phần chịu trách nhiệm chuyển đổi các thao tác GraphQL (Query, Mutation, Subscription) thành dữ liệu thực tế.

children.label: Object Types
children.description: Định nghĩa các kiểu đối tượng trong GraphQL schema bằng cách sử dụng decorator @ObjectType() và @Field().

children.label: Mutations
children.description: Các thao tác được sử dụng để thay đổi dữ liệu phía server, sử dụng decorator @Mutation() và @InputType().

children.label: Subscriptions
children.description: Tính năng đẩy dữ liệu thời gian thực từ server tới client thông qua kết nối persistent channel.

children.label: GraphQL WS Protocol
children.description: Cấu hình giao thức WebSocket cho Subscriptions sử dụng thư viện graphql-ws hoặc subscriptions-transport-ws.

children.label: Scalars
children.description: Các kiểu dữ liệu nguyên tử ở lá của GraphQL query, hỗ trợ các kiểu mặc định và định nghĩa custom scalar.

children.label: Directives
children.description: Các chỉ thị đính kèm vào trường hoặc fragment để thay đổi hành vi thực thi của query hoặc schema.

children.label: Interfaces
children.description: Các kiểu trừu tượng định nghĩa một tập hợp các trường mà một Object Type bắt buộc phải có khi implement.

children.label: Unions & Enums
children.description: Định nghĩa kiểu Union để trả về các kiểu dữ liệu khác nhau từ một trường duy nhất mà không cần chung trường.

children.label: Mapped Types
children.description: Các hàm tiện ích như PartialType, PickType, OmitType giúp tái sử dụng và biến đổi các DTOs/InputTypes.

children.label: Field Middleware
children.description: Cho phép chạy mã tùy ý trước hoặc sau khi một trường cụ thể được resolve.

children.label: Plugins
children.description: Mở rộng chức năng cốt lõi của Apollo Server hoặc Mercurius bằng cách lắng nghe các sự kiện trong vòng đời request.

children.label: CLI Plugin
children.description: Plugin nâng cao quá trình biên dịch TypeScript để tự động thêm decorators và giảm thiểu boilerplate code.

children.label: Complexity
children.description: Định nghĩa độ phức tạp của các trường và giới hạn các truy vấn vượt quá mức độ phức tạp tối đa cho phép.

children.label: Extensions
children.description: Tính năng cấp thấp cho phép đính kèm metadata tùy ý vào cấu hình của các trường hoặc class.

children.label: Generating SDL
children.description: Sử dụng GraphQLSchemaBuilderModule để tạo thủ công file GraphQL SDL schema mà không cần chạy toàn bộ ứng dụng.

children.label: Sharing Models
children.description: Sử dụng model shim để chia sẻ các TypeScript models với ứng dụng frontend mà không bị ảnh hưởng bởi các decorators phía backend.

children.label: Federation
children.description: Chia nhỏ monolithic GraphQL server thành các microservices độc lập và hợp nhất chúng qua một Gateway.

children.label: Other Features & Enhancers
children.description: Sử dụng các tính năng tiêu chuẩn của NestJS như Guards, Interceptors, Filters, và Pipes trong môi trường GraphQL.

children.label: GqlExecutionContext
children.description: Chuyển đổi ExecutionContext tiêu chuẩn thành GqlExecutionContext để truy cập các tham số đặc thù của GraphQL.

children.label: Microservices
children.description: NestJS native support for microservice architectural style of development, utilizing non-HTTP transport layers for communication.

children.description: Core concepts of NestJS microservices, including the installation of the microservices package and bootstrapping using NestFactory.

children.label: Request-Response Style
children.description: A messaging style suitable for exchanging messages between different external services where a response is expected.

children.label: Event-Based Style
children.description: A messaging style used for publishing events without waiting for a response, ideal for fire-and-forget scenarios.

children.label: ClientProxy
children.description: An abstraction used to exchange messages or publish events to a remote Nest microservice.

children.label: Built-in Transporters
children.description: Out-of-the-box transport layer implementations responsible for transmitting messages between microservice instances.

children.label: TCP Transporter
children.description: The default transport layer for NestJS microservices, utilizing raw TCP connections.

children.label: Redis Transporter
children.description: A transporter leveraging Redis Pub/Sub messaging paradigm for fire-and-forget message exchange.

children.label: gRPC Transporter
children.description: A high-performance RPC framework using Protocol Buffers (.proto files) to dynamically bind clients and servers.

children.label: RabbitMQ Transporter
children.description: An open-source message broker transporter supporting multiple messaging protocols and advanced queue configurations.

children.label: Kafka Transporter
children.description: A distributed streaming platform transporter designed for high-throughput, low-latency real-time data feeds.

children.label: MQTT Transporter
children.description: A lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol optimized for low-bandwidth, high-latency networks and IoT.

children.label: NATS Transporter
children.description: A simple, secure, and high-performance messaging system for cloud-native applications and microservices.

children.label: Custom Transporters
children.description: API and strategies allowing developers to build custom transport layers or extend existing ones.

children.description: An interface implemented by custom transporter classes to manage server lifecycle methods like listen and close.

children.label: Exception Filters
children.description: Exception handling layer for microservices, utilizing RpcException instead of HttpException.

children.label: RpcException
children.description: The dedicated exception class thrown within NestJS microservices to propagate errors.

children.label: Pipes
children.description: Data validation and transformation components adapted for microservices, throwing RpcException on failure.

children.label: Guards
children.description: Authorization and permission components for microservices, throwing RpcException on access denial.

children.label: Interceptors
children.description: Aspect-oriented programming components used to bind extra logic before or after microservice message execution.

children.description: Grouping controllers into logical sections, with support for hierarchical tags in OpenAPI 3.2.

children.label: @ApiResponse & Shorthands
children.description: Defining HTTP response codes and schemas using @ApiResponse or shorthand decorators like @ApiOkResponse.

children.description: Decorators like @ApiBearerAuth, @ApiBasicAuth, @ApiOAuth2, and @ApiCookieAuth to secure specific operations.

children.label: Mapped Types

children.description: Generates a new type with all properties of the input class set to optional.

children.label: PickType & OmitType
children.description: Constructs new types by either picking specific properties or omitting a set of keys from an input class.

children.description: An opt-in TypeScript compilation plugin that automatically annotates DTOs and reduces boilerplate code.

children.label: Other Features
children.description: Advanced configurations including global prefixes, global parameters, global responses, and multiple specifications.
